summary: SentinelPay prod: cache invalidation during canary rollback caused semantic mismatches, spike in 5xx, and billing anomaly
description: Issue summary: SentinelPay observed elevated 5xx errors, unexpected semantic drift in generation outputs, and an unexplained billing spike starting 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC. Impact: customer production checkout flows returned malformed/irrelevant prompts and experienced API errors for ~45 minutes. Environment: prod (us-east-1), enterprise Dedicated + routing through canary pool. Immediate customer impact: checkout failures for ~1.2% of requests and two SLO breaches. This ticket captures the incident, investigation, mitigation, and follow-up actions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route customer traffic to canary variant (rollout step 3). 2) Execute high-concurrency embed + generation flows (checkout flow with prefill + semantic ranking). 3) Observe intermittent 500 responses, increased tail latency, and embedding mismatches. Note: reproduces only when canary rollback script is triggered with 'purge-cache --pattern=\"prefix:customer-*\"' against the shared cache cluster.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: During canary rollback we invoked a cache purge job to remove corrupted prefixes. Due to a bug in the purge utility, the glob pattern matched customer-specific kv namespaces across the shared cluster, resulting in mass invalidation. This caused requests to miss cached embeddings/prefix KV, forcing runtime to recompute embeddings and route to larger model variants for safety, which increased per-token cost and briefly pushed some request paths into error states (timeouts + backend retries). We verified: (a) purge logs show pattern 'prefix:customer-*' executed across nodes; (b) KV checksums show reset to zeros for affected keys; (c) repopulation flow restored embeddings and removed checksum errors. Root cause: insufficient isolation of purge jobs in canary rollback script + missing dry-run guard + overly-permissive cache key naming convention. Secondary contributor: routing fallback had no per-customer throttle when cache population lagged, causing load on fallback models and billing surge.
resolution: Mitigation applied: 1) Immediately disabled purge job and re-enabled pinned cache-serving nodes for SentinelPay. 2) Throttled routing to fallback models for SentinelPay to cap token surge. 3) Triggered prioritized cache repopulation using customer snapshot to restore semantic embeddings. 4) Conducted controlled rollback with dry-run verification. Impact remediation completed by 2026-03-10T02:56 UTC. Customer notified and credits applied for abnormal billing. Engineering deployed a hotfix to purge utility to require explicit namespace flag and added a dry-run confirmation step.

Final resolution email 2026-03-10T03:20 UTC with apology, summary of actions, and confirmation of billing credit. Follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC to review long-term mitigations and SLA implications.
next_steps: 1) Require namespace-scoped purge flags and add protective dry-run by default (owner: eng/cache, due 2026-03-17). 2) Introduce per-customer fallback throttles and token caps (owner: serving-runtime, due 2026-04-01). 3) Rename cache key prefixes to include instance-scoped hash to avoid accidental cross-tenant purges (owner: infra, due 2026-03-31). 4) Run incident tabletop with CSM/SRE/Eng and SentinelPay on 2026-03-12. 5) Add automated canary pre-check that simulates cache purge in a shadow cluster before allowing rollback (owner: release-engineering, due 2026-04-07).
follow_up_actions: Ticket created INT-1212 to implement purge utility hardening. Billing team ticket SUP-60001 created to process credits for SentinelPay. Engineering PR referenced for hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2173. Confluence postmortem published and linked.
